one_month_reasoning: The Q3 2026 report is scheduled for 22 October 2026, inside the window that ends 2026-11-05 (Nokia financial calendar, source 8; Q2 release, source 2). Management already guided Q3 net sales +3% to +7% q/q (EUR 4.96-5.15bn) and comparable operating profit 'largely flat' vs Q2's EUR 434m because software revenue moved from Q3 into Q2, with Mobile Infrastructure gross margin guided down to 44-46% (sources 2,3). The Infront consensus of 4 Aug (EUR 5,051m sales, EUR 444m OP, EUR 0.06 EPS; source 7) sits on that guided path, so the headline beat/miss is likely small. What moves the stock is (a) AI & Cloud order intake after a lumpy EUR 2.8bn Q2 that management said should not repeat every quarter, (b) whether FY26 'somewhat above the midpoint of EUR 2.1-2.6bn' is kept and any early 2027 colour, (c) memory/component cost and supply commentary. Q2 showed the stock can fall on a beat (it fell from ~$10.1 to ~$9.1 in the week of the report). EDGAR shows no guidance-related 6-K since 23 July (source 14). Today's +6% move came with no company filing; I take no drift from it. Monthly vol = 62%/3.5 = ~17.7%; I use a lognormal centred on ~$10.85 with sigma 0.17 (earnings in window keeps it near full monthly vol), giving P(>=10.84) = 0.50. FX matters too: the ADR moves 1:1 with EUR/USD (1.1269 ECB, source 15).

fair_value.method: Blend of 60% forward P/E (NTM EPS at Oct-2027 EUR 0.393 x 23x = EUR 9.04 = $10.18 at EUR/USD 1.1269) and 40% SOTP on 2028E (NI NOPAT EUR 1.23bn x 30 + MI NOPAT EUR 1.18bn x 16.6 - common EUR 2.2bn + net cash EUR 2.78bn = EUR 56.9bn / 5.80bn sh = EUR 9.81 = $11.05). Blended $10.53, ~3% below the $10.84 close.

bear.story: AI & Cloud orders prove pulled forward (Q2's EUR 2.8bn was 'lumpy', partly long-dated supply-securing orders), memory/component inflation squeezes margins, telecom RAN stays flat; 2027 OP ~EUR 2.3bn, EPS ~EUR 0.31 x 19x = EUR 5.9 = ~$6.6-6.8; the AI premium largely disappears and the stock trades back to its Dec-2025/Jan-2026 levels ($6-7).

base.story: Guidance met 'somewhat above midpoint' in 2026; NI grows ~15% in 2027 with margin moving to the 13% low end of the CMD target; MI flat around EUR 1.55bn; 2028E OP ~EUR 3.1bn (upper half of EUR 2.7-3.2bn target). Market pays ~23x NTM EPS EUR 0.39 -> ~$10.2-11.

bull.story: San Jose InP fab ramps on time (volume production by end-2026), AI & Cloud backlog converts and NI grows 25%+ with margins toward 15-17% in 2027; 2028E OP > EUR 3.5bn, EPS ~EUR 0.47; the market re-rates NI toward optical peers (~30x group) -> ~$15.9, near the June 2026 high of $17.45.

comps_summary.peer_range: Fwd P/E 14.7x (HPE) to 51.6x (LITE); EV/EBITDA (LTM, as published by source) 8.1x (ERIC) to 123.9x (LITE). Bimodal: telecom/enterprise cohort median fwd P/E 18.1x, AI-optical cohort median 43.0x.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: 23x NTM P/E (and an implied ~23.6x in the SOTP) is below the 10-peer median of 30.3x and inside the range. NOK currently trades at 23.5x 2027 consensus EPS (EUR 0.41 x 1.1269 = $0.462) and 28.3x 2026 consensus EPS (EUR 0.34).
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: The discount to the median comes from mix, not a call that Nokia will lag. About half of Nokia's 2028E segment profit is Mobile Infrastructure (RAN, core, patent licensing). That business has Ericsson's flat-to-declining growth profile (ERIC fwd P/E 16.6x, EPS growth forecast -6%), and the CMD only targets OP growth 'from a EUR 1.5bn base'. Nokia's AI-exposed Network Infrastructure is valued at 30x, a ~30% discount to the AI-optical cohort median. That discount should hold through the horizon because NI's guided growth (12-14% in 2026; CMD 6-8% CAGR) and margins (H1'26 7.4%, 2028 target 13-17%) are structurally below Ciena, Lumentum, Coherent and Arista, whose forecast EPS growth is 29-88%. Mix-weighting the two cohorts this way gives ~23-24x.

thesis_break_reason: $6.50 = EUR 5.77 at 1.1269, about 14x my 2028E EPS of EUR 0.41. That is an Ericsson-like multiple on the whole company with zero value for the AI & Cloud optical/IP franchise, back to pre-Nvidia/pre-AI-order levels. Trading there would most likely mean something fundamental broke rather than volatility: AI & Cloud orders cancelled or exposed as double-ordering, the FY26 guide cut below EUR 2.1bn, or a 2027 outlook implying no progress toward the EUR 2.7-3.2bn 2028 target.

key_uncertainties: Durability of AI & Cloud orders: Q2'26 EUR 2.8bn intake vs EUR 446m quarterly sales; mgmt says intake is lumpy and partly long-dated supply-securing orders (Bernstein asked about double-ordering).
Supply constraints (memory, leading-edge silicon, InP wafers) cap NI revenue and raise costs; mgmt expects shortages to persist and the new Arizona fab to add capacity only from ~2029.
Mobile Infrastructure is half of profit and flat; AI-RAN shift to general-purpose silicon (NVIDIA) could disrupt the ~EUR 3bn mobile R&D base and margins before volume arrives in 2028.
Cash conversion: FY26 FCF now tracking the low end of 55-75%, H1'26 FCF -EUR 104m, restructuring charges raised to EUR 800m in 2026.
FX: reporting is in EUR, so the ADR moves with EUR/USD (1.1269 now vs 1.14 assumed in the outlook); USD-based AI & Cloud revenue translates differently.

Defense exposure is small and not separately disclosed. 'Mission Critical Enterprise & Defense' was EUR 448m in Q2'26 (-3% y/y) and EUR 914m in H1'26 (~9.9% of sales, source 1). The Nokia Defense incubation unit (sources 4,5) and the ICEYE sovereign-LEO partnership (first satellites expected 2028, source 13) are optionality, not in the numbers.
Multiple regime: the stock went $6 to $17.45 to $9 in 2026; 62% realized vol means sentiment on AI-optical names dominates fundamentals over 12 months.
reasoning: Primary-lane build. (1) Facts from filings: Q2'26 sales EUR 4,815m (+9% cc), comparable OP EUR 434m (9.0%), comp. diluted EPS EUR 0.07, net cash EUR 2,776m, FCF -EUR 732m; NI +12% (Optical +20%, IP +16%), AI & Cloud sales EUR 446m (+105%), orders EUR 2.8bn; FY26 guide EUR 2.1-2.6bn, tracking 'somewhat above midpoint'; FCF conversion now at the low end of 55-75%; restructuring charges raised to EUR 800m (sources 1-3). CMD 2028 target OP EUR 2.7-3.2bn, NI margin 13-17%, MI from EUR 1.5bn base, common EUR 150m (source 4). (2) My 2027E/2028E OP of EUR 2.70bn/3.12bn gives EPS of EUR 0.35/0.41. That is below the 2027 consensus of EUR 0.41 (source 16), which pulls the CMD endpoint a year forward; I don't, because supply limits NI growth until the San Jose fab ramps. (3) Valuation: 23x NTM EPS (inside a bimodal 10-peer range, median 30.3x) blended with a SOTP (NI 30x, MI at Ericsson 16.6x) gives fair value $10.53 at EUR/USD 1.1269 (ECB), against $10.84 now. Analyst average PT $14.97 (source 16) is noted as evidence, not used. (4) Base rate: 62% realized vol, and the stock tripled then halved within 2026. The ladder mixes three scenario lognormals (bear $6.75 / base $10.50 / bull $15.75 at 25/50/25%) with a single lognormal (median $10.5, sigma 0.52) for fat tails. That gives a median of ~$10.7, P(>=$10.84) = 0.48, P(>=$6.50) = 0.86, P(>=$16.26) = 0.16. Post-Q2 insider buying by a board member and several senior managers at EUR 7.84-8.45 (sources 11,12) is mildly supportive but not used in numbers. Unverified secondary items (index re-entry, UK C3IA defense MoU, CEO media remarks) were left out of the valuation. Source mix: 14 of 26 sources are primary filings, releases and transcripts. The other 12 are market-data pages that the mandated 10-peer comp table and the FX rate require (one per peer), which pulls the in-lane share to ~54%. Excluding those mandated data pages, the research itself is ~93% primary. Option prices and IV were not consulted.
